name: Refugee Status Determination

requirements.blocker_text: Act No. 21/91 (Refugee Act) and Decree No. 32/2007 (procedural regulation) govern refugee status determination. The National Institute for Refugee Support (INAR) handles applications in coordination with the Ministerial Council for Refugees (CCR) and the Ministry of the Interior. Mozambique is party to the 1951 Refugee Convention, its 1967 Protocol, and the 1969 OAU Convention. Asylum applicants receive provisional identification valid for 2 years, renewable every 6 months, extending to family members. Recognized refugees receive an identity document and a travel document (valid 2 years) when needing to leave the country. INAR can restrict an applicant's movement 'if deemed necessary,' and documents may be withheld on national-security or public-order grounds. Rejected applicants may appeal to the Administrative Court. This dataset could not confirm specific work or education rights for recognized refugees from the sources fetched.
requirements.fix_path: File a refugee status claim; initial screening by immigration authorities refers the case to INAR for material and legal assistance. This dataset could not confirm the exact filing deadline or registration steps.

outcome.duration_length: provisional identification 2 years, renewable every 6 months, pending final determination; recognized refugees receive an identity document and 2-year travel document

sources.title: UNHCR Rights Mapping and Analysis Platform -- Act No. 21/91 (Refugee Act): INAR/CCR determination process, provisional and final documentation, movement restrictions, appeal to the Administrative Court

STATUS: DRAFT -- both sources are tier 2 (a UNHCR-run legal-text platform hosting the actual Mozambican Refugee Act and its implementing decree, not .gov.mz domains); the validator requires tier-1 sourcing for a hard requirement before publishing. This is a genuinely solid, real domestic framework -- a real named law (21/91), a real implementing decree (32/2007), and two real government bodies (INAR, CCR) -- joining the positive-framework pattern found for Paraguay, Bolivia, and Cameroon earlier in this dataset, rather than the 'no domestic law at all' pattern found for Haiti, Cuba, Afghanistan, or Libya. work_rights/study_rights set to 'restricted' as a conservative default since this dataset's sources described documentation and movement/appeal provisions in detail but did not specify employment or education rights explicitly -- a genuine, disclosed gap rather than an assumed 'full' or 'none.'
